claims.text: The durability of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts during ethanol oxidation is governed by sluggish diffusion.
A high-entropy-alloy structure produces a sluggish-diffusion effect.
Sluggish diffusion enhances the structural robustness of the catalyst.
Sluggish diffusion suppresses catalyst particle growth.
Enhanced structural robustness and suppressed particle growth improve catalyst durability.
Introducing an HEA structure will improve catalytic performance relative to conventional catalysts without an HEA structure.
Introducing an HEA structure will improve durability relative to conventional catalysts without an HEA structure.
The proposed mechanism applies under ethanol oxidation reaction conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution is already presented as the HEA catalyst, yet the intervention is introduction of an HEA structure and the experiment proposes PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts both with and without that structure. The structural distinction and the controlled variable needed to create these two states are not defined.
